note: group systems is the closest existing atlas group (rates and responses); the page is chemical kinetics

title.en: Activation energy and the Arrhenius law

description.zh: 反应要翻过一座能量山：只有能量超过山顶的分子才能反应，升温让超过山顶的分子比例指数式增加，所以速率随温度急剧上升（k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT) 中的玻尔兹曼因子）；催化剂不加热，而是把山本身降低，逆反应同理。最简形式，忽略取向因子与熵。
description.en: A reaction must climb an energy hill: only molecules above the top can react, and warming raises that fraction exponentially, so the rate climbs steeply with temperature (the Boltzmann factor in k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT)). A catalyst does not heat things up — it lowers the hill itself, and the reverse reaction follows the same picture. Simplest form, ignoring orientation factors and entropy.

label.zh: 只有分布的尾部起作用
label.en: Only the tail of a distribution matters

reason.zh: 反应速率由能量分布尾部那一小部分分子决定，估计稀有事件需要大量样本。
reason.en: The rate is set by the small tail of the energy distribution, and estimating a rare event takes a very large sample.

reason.zh: 能量足够的分子比例就是一个概率 e^(−Eₐ/RT)，速率常数把这个概率乘上碰撞频率。
reason.en: The fraction of molecules with enough energy is a probability, e^(−Eₐ/RT), and the rate constant multiplies it by a collision frequency.

reason.zh: 放热反应让温度升高、速率变快，可能自我加速，是反馈的化学例子。
reason.en: An exothermic reaction warms itself and speeds up, a chemical example of positive feedback.

title.zh: 为什么升温能让反应快这么多？
title.en: Why does warming speed a reaction up so much?

ask.zh: 只有能量超过能量山的分子才能反应——升温时，超过山顶的分子比例变大还是变小？
ask.en: Only molecules with energy above the hill can react — when temperature rises, does the share above the top grow or shrink?

ask.zh: k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT) 里，T 变大时指数部分怎样变？为什么反应速率对温度这么敏感？
ask.en: In k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT), what happens to the exponent as T grows? Why is the rate so sensitive to temperature?

ask.zh: 如果用随机抽样模拟一群分子的能量，升温后能量分布的形状怎样变？
ask.en: If you simulate a crowd of molecules' energies by random sampling, how does the energy distribution's shape change on warming?

reveal.zh: 升温让超过活化能的分子比例指数式增加，所以速率随温度急剧上升；催化剂则是降低能量山本身。
reveal.en: Warming raises the share of molecules above the activation energy exponentially, so the rate climbs steeply with temperature; a catalyst instead lowers the hill itself.
